```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

})
```

## Gene Annotation with Prokka

I used Prokka to predict and annotate genes in the bacterial genome bins recovered from the black band disease metagenome.

Genome candidates with greater than 15% estimated completeness were selected for annotation.

### Initial annotation

I first tested Prokka on `metabat.5` to confirm the workflow was functioning correctly.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
bin=metabat.5
prokka --cpus 2 --outdir "$bin" --prefix "$bin" "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa"
```

Prokka completed successfully and generated gene annotation files, including protein sequences and predicted gene features.

### Batch annotation

I submitted the remaining selected bins for annotation using a Slurm batch script.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/prokka
sbatch run_prokka.sh
```

The batch analysis was submitted as Slurm job 730. The script skips bins that have already been successfully annotated.

### Interpretation

Gene annotation provides predictions of the genes and potential biological functions present in each genome. These predictions can be used to investigate microbial metabolism, although the presence of a gene does not confirm that it is actively expressed.
